title: IP Network Services: DHCP, DNS and Time

header.html: 3.4 Given a scenario, implement IPv4 and IPv6 network services: dynamic addressing (DHCP reservations, scope, lease time, options, relay and IP helper, exclusions; SLAAC); name resolution (DNS, DNSSEC, DoH and DoT, record types, zone types, authoritative vs non-authoritative, primary vs secondary, recursive, hosts file); time protocols (NTP, PTP, NTS)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1DHCP

Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) assigns IP configuration automatically. The four steps are DORA: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge.

Term Meaning
Scope The range of addresses the server can lease
Exclusions Addresses inside the scope that are never leased (for static devices)
Reservation Always gives the same address to a specific MAC address
Lease time How long a client keeps an address before renewing
Options Extra settings sent to clients: default gateway, DNS servers, domain name
Relay / IP helper A router forwards DHCP broadcasts to a server on another subnet
SLAAC (stateless address autoconfiguration, IPv6) A host builds its own IPv6 address from the router's prefix without a DHCP server
Exam tip

. "DHCP server is on another subnet" = configure a relay (IP helper) on the router. "A printer must always keep the same IP" = a reservation.

2DNS

Domain Name System (DNS) resolves names to IP addresses (port 53).

Record Purpose
A Name to IPv4 address
AAAA Name to IPv6 address
CNAME Alias to another name
MX Mail servers for the domain
TXT Text, verification, SPF/DKIM
NS Authoritative name servers for the zone
PTR IP address to name (reverse lookup)
Concept Meaning
Forward zone / reverse zone Name to address / address to name
Authoritative Holds the zone's records (the source of truth); non-authoritative answers come from a cache
Primary / secondary Primary holds the writable zone; secondary keeps a read-only copy by zone transfer
Recursive resolver Does the full lookup on the client's behalf, asking other servers
DNSSEC Digitally signs records to prove they are authentic (protects integrity, not privacy)
DoH / DoT DNS over HTTPS (port 443) / DNS over TLS (port 853): encrypt DNS queries for privacy
Hosts file A local file of name-to-address mappings, checked before DNS
Exam tip

. DNSSEC proves authenticity; DoH and DoT hide the query. MX = mail; PTR = reverse lookup; CNAME = alias.

3Time protocols

Protocol Notes
NTP (Network Time Protocol) Synchronizes clocks, UDP 123, hierarchy of strata; accurate time matters for logs, certificates and authentication
PTP (Precision Time Protocol) Sub-microsecond accuracy for industrial and financial networks
NTS (Network Time Security) Adds authentication and encryption to NTP
Exam tip

. DHCP relay = IP helper on the router; reservation = fixed address for a MAC; exclusion = never leased.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Clients in a branch subnet cannot get addresses from the central DHCP server. What should be configured on the branch router?

  • AA static route to the DNS server
  • BA DHCP relay (IP helper)
  • CA larger lease time
  • DA PTR record
Show the answer

Answer: B. A relay forwards DHCP broadcasts across subnets.

S2A network printer must always receive the same address from DHCP. What should be created?

  • AA DHCP exclusion
  • BA second scope
  • CA CNAME record
  • DA DHCP reservation
Show the answer

Answer: D. A reservation binds an address to a MAC address.

S3Which DNS record maps a hostname to an IPv6 address?

  • AA
  • BPTR
  • CAAAA
  • DMX
Show the answer

Answer: C. AAAA records hold IPv6 addresses.

S4Which DNS feature proves that a response was not tampered with?

  • ADoH
  • BA hosts file
  • CDNSSEC
  • DA recursive resolver
Show the answer

Answer: C. DNSSEC signs records to prove authenticity.

S5A company wants DNS queries hidden from observers on the network. Which feature fits?

  • ADNS over HTTPS
  • BDNSSEC alone
  • CA reverse zone
  • DA secondary server
Show the answer

Answer: A. DoH encrypts DNS queries.

S6Which protocol keeps device clocks synchronized for accurate log timestamps?

  • ASNMP
  • BLDAP
  • CSMTP
  • DNTP
Show the answer

Answer: D. NTP synchronizes time on UDP 123.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What does DORA stand for?

Show the answer

Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge.

R2What does a PTR record do?

Show the answer

Maps an IP address to a name.

R3What does SLAAC do?

Show the answer

Lets an IPv6 host build its own address from the router's prefix.

R4Which port does NTP use?

Show the answer

UDP 123.

R5What is a DHCP exclusion?

Show the answer

Addresses in the scope that are never leased.

R6What does a recursive resolver do?

Show the answer

Performs the full lookup on the client's behalf.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
DHCP DORA; scope, exclusions, reservation, lease, options, relay; SLAAC for IPv6
DNS records A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, PTR
DNS concepts forward and reverse, authoritative, primary and secondary, recursive, DNSSEC, DoH/DoT, hosts file
Time NTP (UDP 123), PTP (precise), NTS (secure)
